learningObjectives: See the big picture: how Modules, TestCases, Execution, and Requirements link together.
Look up Tosca syntax fast: Buffer, XBuffer, TCP, random values, and dynamic dates.
Recall the most-used keyboard shortcuts to work faster in Tosca Commander.
Apply best-practice rules for a well-structured, maintainable TestCase.
Diagnose identification, expression and reference failures using current documentation and the execution log.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: The Big Picture — How Tosca Sections Connect (Mindmap)

elements.description: Each section owns one job; together they form the automation workflow.
items: Modules — the technical map of the SUT, collected via XScan. To steer a control it must be uniquely identifiable (properties, anchor, parent).
TestCases — a sequence of actions (the path through the application) built from Modules.
Execution — runs TestCases/folders; organize with ExecutionLists; drag a TestCase onto an ExecutionList to create an ExecutionEntry; add Recovery Scenarios to keep runs going.
Requirements — plan test processes and monitor risk coverage (functional & non-functional); TestCases link here.
TestCaseDesign — models test data and combinations; consult its current documentation separately.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Syntax Cheat Sheet — Text Expressions & Random Values

elements.description: Parameterized expressions use braces around the command and brackets around arguments. Some expressions, such as {DATE}, need no arguments; check each command separately.

rows: Reads/buffers the DYNAMIC part of a string. Name may include numbers but must NOT be only numbers

elements.text: Taught in depth in Section 03 (Buffer/MATH/Random), Section 05 (TCP), and Section 08 (XBuffer). This is your one-stop syntax lookup.

bulletPoints: {B[..]} recall a buffer · {XB[..]} buffer a dynamic string part · {CP[..]} config parameter.
RND max 18 digits; RANDOMTEXT max 1024 chars; regex patterns go in double quotes.
XBuffer name can contain numbers but cannot be ONLY numbers.

elements.text: Use {DATE} for the current date or {DATE[][][dd.MM.yyyy]} for explicit formatting. In parameterized unprefixed expressions retain all three slots; prefixed forms omit the format slot. Offset w means workdays, excluding weekends and configured holidays; M means months and m minutes. ADAY and AMONTH return three characters. With a 15 June 2025 base, {MONTHLAST[][-3y][ddMMMyyyy]} displays 30Jun2022. TIME and DATETIME output follows configured formats, not a universal AM/PM layout. Explicit format takes priority over the matching TCP and Settings format.

For table counts, use RowCount->RowNum with ActionMode Buffer, then recall {B[RowNum]}. ColumnCount similarly buffers the column count. Verify the actual table/header representation before subtracting anything. If the measured row count is 5 and exactly one counted row is a header, {MATH[{B[RowNum]}-1]} gives 4 data rows. This subtraction is conditional, not a universal rule for every engine or table.

A Library block reference receives changes from the shared block. Resolve Reference replaces that reference with locally editable TestSteps, so later Library edits no longer change that local copy. Module references and TCP dependencies remain. Resolve only when a deliberate local variation is needed; do not assume a particular save boundary makes Undo available or unavailable.

rows: Create XModule in the applicable Modules context
Search for a TestStep (fuzzy add Module)
Run in the active context; TestCase/TestSteps use ScratchBook, ExecutionList uses execution
Show/hide context-specific objects or values; inspect the View settings

elements.text: Shortcuts depend on the active window and selected object. Consult Commander’s F1 keyboard menu or the current documentation; the same chord can create different objects in different sections.

bulletPoints: Ctrl+T searches and adds a TestStep; Ctrl+N, Ctrl+E creates an ExecutionList.
Ctrl+N, Ctrl+X creates an XModule; Ctrl+N, Ctrl+R creates an RTSB in a Library.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: What Makes a Good TestCase — Best-Practice Job Aid

elements.text: Build a focused, readable test with controlled preconditions, purposeful actions and assertions that establish the expected outcome. WorkState supports planning; Requirement and ExecutionList links provide traceability and execution organization, without requiring Completed before linking. IF and loops are supported: use them deliberately with bounded conditions rather than hiding failures. Scan the controls needed for the intended scope; a valid Module can contain one control or several. Prefer stable, unique identification and descriptive names. These are independent maintenance recommendations, not a verified original Academy job aid.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Troubleshooting — Diagnose Before Changing the Model

elements.text: Error messages are evidence to investigate, not a unique diagnosis. Inspect the log, current SUT state, engine and affected references before changing the model.

rows: Check the active browser, parent scope and identification properties
Use stable discriminators; a wildcard may broaden matches. Close only surplus test tabs intentionally.
No match or a control cannot be steered
Check navigation, visibility, enabled state and current properties
Wait for the expected state within a bounded timeout; rescan only when identification has changed.
Use F9 in the appropriate context or configure displayed ActionModes.
Check command syntax, argument types, escaping and referenced values
Use that command’s documented format; no-argument DATE is valid.
Check exact name and initialization path
Initialize before recall. Buffer Viewer also permits design-time creation/editing.
Compare the value with the documented browser list
Use the supported spelling, for example Edge; a browser choice must suit the installed environment.
Inspect the affected link and available compatible object
Repair or reassign the reference; do not routinely delete the TestCase or Module.
Inspect engine compatibility, control property, log and referenced objects
Use the documented engine/control procedure; a generic exception alone does not identify the cause.
Inspect AutoCalculateRequirements and the blue outdated-values indicator
Select the RequirementSet and Update Outdated Values when calculation is manual.

examPitfalls.title: Command syntax is specific
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Applying one argument pattern to every expression.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: No-argument DATE is valid; parameterized date forms retain their required slots, while prefixed date forms omit the format slot.

examPitfalls.title: Supported conditionals require deliberate design
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Treating IF as forbidden, or using branches to conceal failed assertions.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use supported IF/loops only for a justified path and bound repeated checks.

examPitfalls.title: Unique and stable identification
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Adding a wildcard to an already ambiguous match.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Check match counts and use a stable discriminator within the correct scope.

examPitfalls.title: Count the actual table representation
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Always subtracting a header or using comparison syntax when buffering.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Buffer RowCount->RowNum, inspect which rows were counted, then adjust only for a confirmed counted header.

practiceQuiz.scenario: With a TestCase or its TestSteps selected, which shortcut runs them in ScratchBook?

options.text: F6
F5
F9
Ctrl+R

practiceQuiz.hint: It's a single function key.
practiceQuiz.rationale: F6 runs the selected TestCase/TestSteps in the ScratchBook. F9 hides/unhides unused TestStepValues; F5 is not the ScratchBook run key.

optionExplanations.A: F6 runs the selected TestCase or steps in ScratchBook.
optionExplanations.B: F5 refreshes Commander rather than starting that test.
optionExplanations.C: F9 toggles context-specific visibility rather than execution.
optionExplanations.D: Ctrl+R is not the documented shortcut for this ScratchBook action.

practiceQuiz.scenario: During execution you get: 'More than one control found for action X'. What is the correct fix?

options.text: Delete the TestCase and rebuild it from scratch.
Inspect matches and refine stable identification; rescan if the Module no longer describes the control.
Increase the synchronization timeout.
Press F9 to reveal the control.

practiceQuiz.hint: The control isn't unique on the page.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The error means the control is not unique. Rescan the Module and tighten its identifying properties (or use a wildcard/anchor/parent) so Tosca finds exactly one control.

optionExplanations.A: Rebuilding discards useful model structure without diagnosing the match.
optionExplanations.B: Inspecting matches and repairing identification addresses ambiguous control selection.
optionExplanations.C: A longer timeout cannot choose uniquely between two already matching controls.
optionExplanations.D: Visibility filters in Commander do not disambiguate controls in the SUT.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Unused DoNothing TestStepValues are still in the model but are hidden by the active View filter. How can you reveal them?

options.text: They were deleted by the last run.
The Module lost its ModuleAttributes.
Use F9 in the appropriate context or adjust the displayed ActionModes in View.
The TestCase WorkState is set to Planned.

practiceQuiz.hint: A single key toggles their visibility.
practiceQuiz.rationale: When 'Hide DoNothing' is active, TestStepValues with no action are hidden. F9 (or View -> Show DoNothing) brings them back — nothing was deleted.

optionExplanations.A: The scenario confirms the values remain in the model.
optionExplanations.B: A View filter does not remove ModuleAttribute associations.
optionExplanations.C: Context-specific visibility controls can reveal the filtered values.
optionExplanations.D: WorkState does not decide whether DoNothing values are displayed.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A test fails with 'Buffer with name X was not found'. What is the most likely reason and fix?

options.text: Buffers expire after 24 hours; recreate it daily.
The buffer step runs, but F9 is hiding it.
Buffers only work in ExecutionLists, not ScratchBook.
The buffer was never set before it was used; create it first and match the name exactly (case sensitive).

practiceQuiz.hint: Check initialization and the exact buffer name, including the path actually executed.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Recall needs an existing named buffer. Initialize it before use; Buffer Viewer can also create or edit buffers at design time.

optionExplanations.A: There is no stated daily buffer-expiration mechanism.
optionExplanations.B: A View filter hides model rows, not the buffer value used at execution.
optionExplanations.C: ScratchBook supports buffers too; execution-list membership is not the cause.
optionExplanations.D: A missing buffer must be initialized under the exact name before recall.

practiceQuiz.scenario: AutoCalculateRequirements is Off and a RequirementSet has the blue outdated-values indicator after linked TestCase changes. Which action refreshes the calculated values?

options.text: Select the RequirementSet and run Update Outdated Values.
Re-run the entire ExecutionList.
Delete and re-link the TestCase.
Change the Requirement weight.

practiceQuiz.hint: Refresh calculation explicitly when automatic calculation is disabled.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Manual calculation requires Update Outdated Values on the affected RequirementSet; changing weight or recreating links is not the calculation command.

optionExplanations.A: This explicitly refreshes the stale RequirementSet calculation.
optionExplanations.B: Another run does not substitute for manual calculation when it is Off.
optionExplanations.C: Recreating a TestCase link is unnecessary for recalculating values.
optionExplanations.D: Weight changes alter risk weighting rather than invoke the refresh command.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which statement reflects Tosca best practice for a well-built TestCase?

options.text: Use IF statements liberally to branch logic.
Use clear names, controlled preconditions, meaningful assertions and purposeful links; use supported conditionals only where justified.
Keep each Module to a single control for precision.
Leave TestSteps unnamed to maximize reuse.

practiceQuiz.hint: Aim for clarity and reliable outcomes rather than an arbitrary number of controls.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The goal is a focused maintainable test. IF is supported, Modules may have one control, and Completed is not a prerequisite for traceability links.

optionExplanations.A: Unnecessary branching can obscure intended assertions and increase maintenance.
optionExplanations.B: This emphasizes meaningful outcomes and deliberate use of supported structures.
optionExplanations.C: A fixed one-control rule is not a universal Module design requirement.
optionExplanations.D: Unnamed steps reduce readability; they do not increase technical reuse.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In the Execution section, what do you do to create an ExecutionEntry?

options.text: Right-click the Modules folder and choose 'New Entry'.
Link a Requirement to the ExecutionList.
Drag a TestCase onto an ExecutionList.
Run the ScratchBook.

practiceQuiz.hint: An entry represents one TestCase inside a list.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Dragging a TestCase onto an ExecutionList creates an ExecutionEntry (a runnable reference to that TestCase). Modules hold the SUT map; Requirements track coverage — neither creates an ExecutionEntry.

optionExplanations.A: The Modules section contains technical models rather than execution entries.
optionExplanations.B: Requirement linking supplies coverage traceability rather than this ExecutionEntry.
optionExplanations.C: Dropping a TestCase on an ExecutionList creates its execution reference.
optionExplanations.D: ScratchBook is a quick run and does not create the specified list entry.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Using {RND[n]}, what is the maximum length (number of digits) Tosca allows for the random integer?

options.text: 8 digits
10 digits
Unlimited
18 digits

practiceQuiz.hint: It's a specific two-digit cap in the cheat sheet.
practiceQuiz.rationale: {RND[n]} supports a maximum of 18 digits. For a range instead of a length, use {RND[min][max]} (negatives allowed).

optionExplanations.A: Eight digits is below the documented maximum for the length form.
optionExplanations.B: Ten digits is also below the documented maximum.
optionExplanations.C: The length form has a finite limit rather than unlimited digits.
optionExplanations.D: The documented RND length limit is 18 digits.

practiceQuiz.scenario: You need a random number that includes decimal places (e.g., a 5-digit number with 2 decimals). Which expression is correct?

options.text: {RNDDECIMAL[5][2]}
{RANDOMTEXT[5]}
{DECIMAL[5][2]}

practiceQuiz.hint: There's a dedicated decimal random function.
practiceQuiz.rationale: {RNDDECIMAL[length][decimals]} creates a random number with decimals — {RNDDECIMAL[5][2]} = 5 digits, 2 decimal places. {RND[..]} produces integers only.

optionExplanations.A: RNDDECIMAL accepts the length and decimal-place arguments shown.
optionExplanations.B: Two-argument RND specifies integer bounds, not decimal precision.
optionExplanations.C: RANDOMTEXT generates a string rather than a decimal with the requested precision.
optionExplanations.D: DECIMAL is not the documented random-decimal command.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which statement about {RANDOMTEXT[n]} is correct?

options.text: It generates digits only, up to 18 characters.
It generates a random alphanumeric string, up to a maximum length of 1024.
It only works inside a MATH expression.
It requires a regular expression in double quotes.

practiceQuiz.hint: Letters + numbers, with an upper size limit.
practiceQuiz.rationale: {RANDOMTEXT[n]} produces a random string of letters and numbers, with a maximum length of 1024. The regex-constrained variant is {RANDOMREGEX["pattern"]}.

optionExplanations.A: Digit-only generation describes a different random-number operation.
optionExplanations.B: RANDOMTEXT generates letters and numbers with a maximum length of 1024.
optionExplanations.C: RANDOMTEXT is directly usable as a dynamic expression.
optionExplanations.D: Regex-pattern input belongs to RANDOMREGEX, not RANDOMTEXT length.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is a valid constraint on the name used inside {XB[Name]}?

options.text: The name must be all uppercase.
The name must be exactly 8 characters.
The name may include numbers but must NOT consist only of numbers.
The name must match a Test Configuration Parameter.

practiceQuiz.hint: Numbers are allowed, but not numbers alone.
practiceQuiz.rationale: For XBuffer, the buffer name may include numbers but must not consist ONLY of numbers. The value inside the brackets is the buffer name where the excluded dynamic part is stored.

optionExplanations.A: There is no all-uppercase requirement for this buffer name.
optionExplanations.B: The documented constraint does not impose an eight-character length.
optionExplanations.C: A numeric-only name is disallowed; names may mix letters and digits.
optionExplanations.D: XBuffer naming is separate from naming a configuration parameter.

practiceQuiz.scenario: You must generate a random value that starts with a capital letter, followed by lowercase letters, and ends with exactly four digits. Which expression fits?

options.text: {REGEX[A-Z][a-z][0-9]}

practiceQuiz.hint: A pattern in double quotes needs the regex-aware function.
practiceQuiz.rationale: {RANDOMREGEX["pattern"]} generates a random string constrained by a regular expression (in double quotes). {RANDOMTEXT[n]} takes only a length, not a pattern.

optionExplanations.A: RANDOMTEXT takes a length rather than this regex constraint.
optionExplanations.B: RND takes integer length or bounds rather than a text regex.
optionExplanations.C: This is not the documented random-regex command syntax.
optionExplanations.D: RANDOMREGEX generates a value matching the quoted expression.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In a dynamic date offset such as {DATE[][+4M][MM]}, what does the capital 'M' represent, and how does it differ from lowercase 'm'?

options.text: Capital M = months; lowercase m = minutes.
Capital M = minutes; lowercase m = months.
They are interchangeable.
Capital M = milliseconds; lowercase m = months.

practiceQuiz.hint: Date variables are case sensitive.
practiceQuiz.rationale: In dynamic date offsets, capital M = months and lowercase m = minutes. All dynamic-date variables are case sensitive, so mixing them is a common error.

optionExplanations.A: Case distinguishes month offsets from minute offsets.
optionExplanations.B: This reverses the documented month and minute units.
optionExplanations.C: Case changes meaning; these units are not interchangeable.
optionExplanations.D: Milliseconds use fff rather than capital M.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A table scan reports RowCount = 5, including exactly one header and four item rows. You buffer it with RowCount->RowNum. What is stored, and how do you obtain the item count?

options.text: RowNum = 4; it already excludes the header.
RowNum = 5 (includes the header); use {MATH[{B[RowNum]}-1]} for data rows.
RowNum = 4; add 1 for the header.
RowCount cannot count rows in a cart table.

practiceQuiz.hint: Subtract only the header confirmed to be counted in this scenario.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The measured count is 5; subtract the one known counted header to get 4. Use -> when buffering a table property, and do not generalize the header assumption to other tables.

optionExplanations.A: The measured count in this scenario explicitly includes one header.
optionExplanations.B: Five counted rows minus the one confirmed header gives four item rows.
optionExplanations.C: Adding a header would increase an already header-inclusive count.
optionExplanations.D: RowCount can count the scanned table rows; the issue is representation.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What changes when Resolve Reference is applied to a Reusable TestStepBlock reference?

options.text: It refreshes calculated Requirement weights.
It deletes all shared Library blocks.
It creates locally editable TestSteps that stop receiving Library block edits; Module and TCP dependencies remain.
It creates an independent copy of every Module and TCP.

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish the Library block link from other model dependencies.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Resolve copies the block’s steps for local editing and removes that Library reference. It does not clone all technical/configuration dependencies.

optionExplanations.A: Requirement calculation is separate from resolving a Library reference.
optionExplanations.B: Resolving one reference does not delete the shared block.
optionExplanations.C: The local steps stop receiving shared block edits but retain other dependencies.
optionExplanations.D: Resolve Reference does not clone Modules or all configuration parameters.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which keyboard shortcut opens the fuzzy search to add a TestStep (Module) inside a TestCase?

options.text: F9
F6
Ctrl+N, Ctrl+X
Ctrl+T

practiceQuiz.hint: A single Ctrl+letter, not a chord.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Ctrl+T opens Search and Add TestStep in the TestCase context. F6 runs, F9 changes visibility, and Ctrl+N, Ctrl+X creates an XModule in its applicable context.

optionExplanations.A: F9 controls visibility in the active context.
optionExplanations.B: F6 executes the selected test rather than adding a step.
optionExplanations.C: This chord creates an XModule in the appropriate context.
optionExplanations.D: Ctrl+T opens Search and Add TestStep in the TestCase context.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Most 'create' actions in Tosca are a two-key chord starting with Ctrl+N. Which chord creates a new ExecutionList?

options.text: Ctrl+N, Ctrl+E
Ctrl+N, Ctrl+T
Ctrl+N, Ctrl+F
Ctrl+N, Ctrl+W

practiceQuiz.hint: E for Execution.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Ctrl+N, Ctrl+E creates an ExecutionList. Ctrl+N,Ctrl+F = Folder, Ctrl+N,Ctrl+T = TestCase, Ctrl+N,Ctrl+W = WHILE statement.

optionExplanations.A: The documented ExecutionList creation chord is Ctrl+N, Ctrl+E.
optionExplanations.B: This creates a TestCase in the applicable TestCases context.
optionExplanations.C: This creates a folder in the applicable context.
optionExplanations.D: This creates a WHILE statement rather than an ExecutionList.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which controls should an XScan Module include for a focused automation task?

options.text: Exactly one control, for precision.
The controls needed for the intended scope, which may be one or several.
One control per TestCase that uses it.
As few as possible, ideally none.

practiceQuiz.hint: The official introductory scan can produce a Module with a single link.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Module scope follows the needed controls, not a universal minimum count. Stable identification and appropriate reuse matter more than including every widget.

optionExplanations.A: Exactly one is valid in some scopes, but not a universal rule.
optionExplanations.B: Include the needed controls; either one or several can be appropriate.
optionExplanations.C: Control count does not grow by one for every referencing TestCase.
optionExplanations.D: A Module with no useful controls cannot serve the stated steering task.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A target page title varies, but its stable prefix uniquely distinguishes it from all other open test tabs. What identification adjustment can accommodate the variable suffix?

options.text: Increase the synchronization timeout.
Delete the TestCase and rebuild it.
Use a wildcard for the variable suffix and confirm that the resulting title match remains unique.
Press F9 to reveal the tab.

practiceQuiz.hint: Allow variation without broadening the match to other tabs.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A wildcard can match a varying suffix, but uniqueness must be confirmed. If it matches multiple tabs, refine the scope or another stable property.

optionExplanations.A: Timing cannot fix an already loaded title that does not match the identification.
optionExplanations.B: The failure does not justify deleting the whole TestCase.
optionExplanations.C: The stable prefix and verified uniqueness make a suffix wildcard appropriate here.
optionExplanations.D: Commander’s View filters do not change browser-tab identification.

practiceQuiz.scenario: The Browser TCP is intended to select Microsoft Edge, but contains an unsupported browser value. Which correction follows the documented browser list?

options.text: TCPs cannot set the browser.
Wrap the browser name as {CP[Edge]} in the Browser value.
The TCP must be defined at the folder level.
Set the Browser TCP to the documented value Edge.

practiceQuiz.hint: A supported browser value is distinct from the syntax used to recall a TCP.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Edge is a documented Browser TCP value. CP recalls a named configuration parameter; it does not turn an unsupported browser value into a valid one.

optionExplanations.A: The Browser TCP is specifically used to select a supported browser.
optionExplanations.B: CP syntax recalls a parameter, not the literal supported Browser value.
optionExplanations.C: Browser TCP validity is not restricted to definition at a folder.
optionExplanations.D: Edge is the documented value for the browser named in this scenario.

quickRecap.value: Use command-specific syntax; no-argument DATE is valid. w counts workdays and M/m distinguish months/minutes.
Buffer RowCount->RowNum; adjust only for headers actually counted.
Local step edits become independent of the Library block; Module and TCP dependencies remain.
Active context matters: Ctrl+T adds a step, Ctrl+N/Ctrl+X creates XModule, F6 runs and F9 changes visibility.
Use readable names, stable identification and purposeful assertions; conditionals are supported.
Investigate the execution log and current references before deleting or rebuilding model objects.
